sentences.text: Longosuchus is an extinct genus of desmatosuchin aetosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in North America.
This reptile measured approximately 3 meters in length.
The species was originally named T. meadei in 1947 based on skeletal remains found in the Otis Chalk quarries in Howard County, western Texas.
Hunt and Lucas renamed the species Longosuchus in 1990 after recognizing it as distinct from Typothorax and honoring Robert Long.
Longosuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae and belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
The parent group of Longosuchus is the tribe Desmatosuchini.
Longosuchus lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
Fossils reported from Morocco are likely misidentified scutes belonging to a paratypothoracin aetosaur rather than Longosuchus.
